content.user_title: Build Auditable Data Resource Cost Schedules
content.value_statement: Organizations often lack a consistent method to identify and support data-resource costs. This skill structures classification, stage assessment, allocation, and evidence planning.
actual_capabilities: Classifies spending as direct labor, direct materials, direct expenses, or indirect expenses.
Separates research-stage costs from potentially capitalizable development-stage costs.
Compares direct attribution, allocation, and reference estimation methods.
Designs allocation rules using labor hours, data volume, usage frequency, or benefit ratios.
Creates evidence checklists linking costs to payroll, invoices, contracts, and time records.
Outlines cost schedules, capitalization summaries, and accounting policy recommendations.
limitations: It does not replace advice from licensed accountants, auditors, tax professionals, or regulators.
It cannot verify source records unless the user provides complete and accurate evidence.
It does not guarantee that a cost qualifies for capitalization or passes an audit.
Its guidance focuses on Chinese data-resource accounting and may not fit other jurisdictions.

use_cases.title: Prepare a cost inventory
use_cases.description: Map ledger items to cost categories, exclusions, periods, and supporting records before closing the accounts.

use_cases.title: Define project allocation rules
use_cases.description: Choose a consistent basis for splitting shared team, cloud, and service costs across data projects.

use_cases.title: Review capitalization evidence
use_cases.description: Test stage boundaries, capitalization conditions, calculations, and document references before formal assurance work.

prompt_templates.title: Classify basic costs
prompt_templates.prompt: Classify these data-project expenses into the four cost categories or exclusions: [expense list]. Explain each decision and identify missing evidence.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a short expense list

prompt_templates.title: Assess project stages
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this project timeline: [timeline]. Separate research and development periods, test the five capitalization conditions, and list evidence needed for each conclusion.

prompt_templates.title: Design an allocation method
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare labor hours, data volume, usage frequency, and benefit ratios for [shared costs]. Recommend a basis, formula, controls, and consistency rules.

prompt_templates.title: Plan an audit-ready attribution
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an end-to-end cost attribution plan for [data resource]. Include scope, stage gates, collection tables, formulas, evidence indexes, checks, and unresolved judgments.

output_examples.input: Classify payroll, cloud hosting, feasibility research, and staff training for a customer data platform.
output: Development payroll: direct labor, subject to time records and the capitalization start date.
Development cloud hosting: direct expense when usage is traceable to the platform.
Feasibility research: research-stage expense, not capitalized.
General staff training: excluded from the data-resource cost base.

output_examples.input: Choose an allocation basis for one engineering team supporting three data products.
output_examples.output: Use approved labor hours when work logs reliably identify effort by product. Document exceptions, review rates monthly, and reconcile allocated hours to payroll.

output_examples.input: List the evidence needed to support a capitalization start date.
output: Approved project initiation or technical feasibility decision.
Evidence of intended completion and planned use or sale.
A reliable method for measuring development expenditure.

best_practices: Define the cost object, capitalization dates, currency, and reporting period before collecting records.
Prefer direct attribution and use documented, consistent allocation methods only for shared costs.
Link every included amount to source evidence and record unresolved judgments separately.
anti_patterns: Do not capitalize research, routine maintenance, training, advertising, or unsupported management costs.
Do not use valuation estimates as substitutes for actual cost in initial measurement.
Do not change allocation methods to increase a preferred capitalization amount.

faq.question: Does this skill provide an official accounting opinion?
faq.answer: No. It supports analysis and documentation, but qualified professionals must approve accounting treatment and assurance conclusions.

faq.question: Can all data-team payroll be capitalized?
faq.answer: No. Only supported development work may qualify, subject to stage, participation, measurement, and applicable accounting requirements.

faq.question: Which allocation method is best?
faq.answer: Direct attribution is preferred. For shared costs, choose the method that best represents consumption and can be applied consistently.

faq.question: Are invoices required for every cost?
faq.answer: External purchases generally need contracts and invoices. Payroll can use payroll, social insurance, assignment, and time records.

faq.question: Can earlier costs be reconstructed?
faq.answer: They may be analyzed, but recognition depends on effective dates, reliable records, and applicable rules against retrospective adjustment.

faq.question: What should I provide first?
faq.answer: Provide the resource scope, project timeline, approvals, ledger details, payroll, time records, contracts, invoices, cloud bills, and current accounting policy.
